## Scenario context

Decoupling services requires choosing between transient message queues (point-to-point) and persistent event streams (commit logs).
* **Behavior**: Messages are placed in the queue, consumed by a single worker, and immediately deleted.
* **Pattern**: Work queue distribution.

```text
Publisher ──► [ Message Queue ] ──► Worker A (Deletes on Ack)
                                ──► Worker B (Round Robin)
```

This walkthrough focuses on **Core Mechanism & Implementation**.

Before making a design choice, clarify:

- Behavior : Messages are placed in the queue, consumed by a single worker, and immediately deleted.
- Pattern : Work queue distribution.

**Concepts in play:** message-queues, event-driven-architecture, stack-and-queue-data-structures, jvm-internals-and-garbage-collection

## Stage 1 — Production Considerations & Trade-offs

- Event Stream (e.g., Apache Kafka) Behavior : Events are appended to a persistent, immutable partition log.
- Consumers track their progress using offsets and can replay events at any time.
- Pattern : Pub-sub, event sourcing, stream processing.

*Applies **message-queues** to the decision above.*

```text
             Immutable Commit Log:
Publisher ──► [ Evt 1 | Evt 2 | Evt 3 | Evt 4 ]
                         ▲               ▲
                         │               │
                   Consumer A (Off: 2)   Consumer B (Off: 4)
```

**Observable outcome:** Pattern : Pub-sub, event sourcing, stream processing.

## End-to-end outcome

Behavior : Messages are placed in the queue, consumed by a single worker, and immediately deleted.

## Alternatives considered

The source focuses on one primary design. A second architecture is not compared, so no alternative is invented here.
